sources.//: This `exclude` list is the template engine's own default list MINUS `**/*.lock.json`, and it exists to keep that one pattern off (FS.GG.Templates#380). The default is not inert: it silently stripped every committed `packages.lock.json` out of each generated workspace, so the reviewed lock could never reach a product. Combined with `Directory.Build.props`'s `RestorePackagesWithLockFile=true`, the product's FIRST restore then AUTHORED its own lock from whatever the ambient host happened to resolve, and `RestoreLockedMode=true` enforced that unreviewed lock forever after — surfacing as `NU1403: Package content hash validation failed` the moment the ambient content moved. This template did not RED on #380 only because `build.sh` runs its npm steps before the locked restore and its solution has fewer restore passes to disagree across; the defect was identical. Declaring `exclude` here REPLACES the engine default wholesale, so every other default pattern below must be restated verbatim; they are copied from the engine's own defaults (dotnet SDK 10.0.302, Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Orchestrator.RunnableProjects). `**/node_modules/**` IS NOT ONE OF THOSE DEFAULTS, and an earlier draft of this comment said it was (FS.GG.Templates#386). The `strings -el` reading that put it among them is a false positive — it sits adjacent to the six real defaults in the binary's string pool, not in the effective list. MEASURED on dotnet SDK 10.0.302 by instantiating a template that declares no `sources` block at all, with one file per claimed pattern seeded at two depths: `bin`, `obj`, `.template.config`, `*.filelist`, `*.user` and `*.lock.json` were filtered at BOTH depths; `node_modules/` was DELIVERED at both. So this line is a NEW guard that never existed — the engine never protected this template, and this is an npm workspace with three `package.json` roots (`Web/`, `Web.Tests/`, `Browser.Tests/`). Measured for this template specifically: a package packed with `Web/node_modules/` present delivered it into the product. `**/.nuget/**` is the ONE pattern in this list that is NOT an engine default, and it is added deliberately (#386): the very `RestorePackagesPath` this template sets (#382) means the regeneration command this template's README documents materializes a workspace-local package folder INSIDE the template source — measured at 75M — and the engine, which knows nothing about that property, delivered it into every generated product. The four templates' lists are identical by intent; `tests/composition/lib/content-exclusions.sh` reds if any of them stops filtering either directory.
